current_answer: Choose a ready-made frontend skill by task, host and required tools, not name or install count. Start with project components and tokens when an existing design system governs the work. Record the installed source and local edits. If using Vercel Skills, an “up to date” global-update message does not verify installed files, and a reported copy-mode update can change file layout; inspect the actual files after updating. None of our sixteen listings has a pool-run outcome comparison against a careful no-skill brief.

catalogue_card.question: Does “up to date” mean your frontend skill is unchanged?
catalogue_card.text: Not for the inspected Vercel Skills global-update path: it compares upstream with a lock entry, not installed files. If you made local edits, inspect the actual files after updating. We did not run the CLI.

summary: Choose a skill by task, host and required tools; use project components and tokens when they govern the screen.
Record the source revision, install scope and local edits before updating a skill.
For Vercel Skills, an “up to date” global status does not verify installed bytes; inspect actual files and link type after update.
Compare consequential task outcomes with a careful no-skill brief on the same project.
uncertainty: The update behavior is based on inspected current source and user reports; this pool did not run the CLI.
The global-update finding does not establish the behavior of every source, version or project-scoped path.
No listed skill has a pool-run no-skill comparison; first-party pool analytics are unavailable.
